objectives: Apply cross-entropy, KL, MI to ML losses.

slides.title: Cross-entropy + maximum likelihood (the classification connection)
slides.body:
**Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)**: choose parameters θ that maximize P(data | θ). For iid data:

  θ* = argmax ∑ log P(x_i | θ) = argmin -∑ log P(x_i | θ) = argmin H(P_true, P_θ)

This is **cross-entropy minimization**.

For classification: P_θ(x) = softmax over classes; cross-entropy = ∑ -y_i log p_θ(x_i). Standard CE loss.

During training:
- L = cross-entropy(P_data, P_model)
- Reduces to: L = H(P_data) + KL(P_data || P_model)
- H(P_data) constant in θ → minimizing CE = minimizing KL

**Implications**:
- CE loss is theoretically optimal (achieves MLE).
- Gradient: ∇L ∝ (p_model - y) — clean, never saturates.
- Calibration: well-trained CE network produces calibrated probabilities.
- Generalization: ML theory + PAC-Bayes connect CE risk to test error.

**Regression with Gaussian noise**: assume y = f(x) + N(0, σ²). MLE = MSE minimization. Same principle, different distribution.

**Cross-entropy variants**:
- **Binary CE**: binary classification.
- **Sparse CE**: integer labels (not one-hot).
- **Focal loss** (Lin+ 2017): downweights easy examples; (1-p)^γ factor; useful for imbalanced + dense prediction.
- **Label smoothing**: target 1-ε on true + ε/(K-1) on others; reduces overconfidence.
- **Distillation**: CE between student + teacher's softmax (with temperature).
- **Knowledge distillation**: KL between distributions.

**Connection to softmax**: softmax is the maximum-entropy distribution given linear scores. Pair softmax + CE for optimization-friendly + theoretically-grounded classifier.

slides.title: ELBO + variational inference + VAEs
slides.body:
**Variational inference**: approximate intractable posterior p(z | x) with simpler q_φ(z | x). Minimize KL(q || p).

**Evidence Lower BOund (ELBO)**:

  log p(x) = E_q[log p(x, z)] - E_q[log q(z | x)] + KL(q || p)
  ≥ E_q[log p(x, z)] - E_q[log q(z | x)]   (=ELBO)

Maximizing ELBO = maximizing log p(x) (since KL ≥ 0 + KL = 0 iff q = p_post). Provides lower bound on data likelihood.

Rearranging:

  ELBO = E_q[log p(x | z)] - KL(q(z | x) || p(z))
        = [reconstruction term] - [regularization term]

Reconstruction: model should reconstruct data well from latent z.
Regularization: q(z | x) should stay close to prior p(z) (often N(0, I)).

**Variational Autoencoder (VAE)** (Kingma + Welling 2013):
- Encoder q_φ(z | x): outputs μ, σ for Gaussian over z.
- Decoder p_θ(x | z): reconstructs x.
- Reparameterization trick: z = μ + σ × ε, ε ~ N(0, I); allows gradient flow.
- Train with ELBO maximization (Adam on -ELBO).

Applications: generative modeling, representation learning, disentanglement, semi-supervised.

**Beyond VAEs**:
- **Normalizing flows**: invertible transformations of Gaussian → flexible distributions; exact log-likelihood. RealNVP, Glow, FFJORD.
- **Diffusion models**: train to reverse noising process; conditional generation. Stable Diffusion + DALL-E 2 + Sora.
- **β-VAE** (Higgins+ 2017): scale KL term by β > 1; encourages disentanglement.
- **InfoVAE / WAE**: alternative divergences (MMD, Wasserstein).
- **Conditional VAEs**: condition on labels.

**Connection to compression**: VAE encoder ≈ source coder; decoder ≈ source decoder; ELBO ≈ negative bit-rate + reconstruction quality. Neural compression literature directly uses VAE-style architectures.

slides.title: Contrastive learning + InfoNCE
slides.body:
**Contrastive learning**: learn representations by distinguishing positive (similar) pairs from negative (dissimilar) pairs.

**InfoNCE loss** (van den Oord+ 2018):

  L = -log [exp(f(x, x⁺)/τ) / ∑_{x'∈{x⁻}} exp(f(x, x')/τ)]

Where:
- (x, x⁺): positive pair (same instance, augmented).
- {x⁻}: negative samples.
- f: similarity (often cosine).
- τ: temperature.

**InfoNCE = MI lower bound** (van den Oord+ 2018 derivation): minimizing InfoNCE upper-bounds the MI between input + representation across positive pairs.

**Architectures + applications**:

• **SimCLR** (Chen+ 2020): same-image augmentations as positives; in-batch negatives. ResNet → projection head. Foundational self-supervised method.
• **MoCo** (He+ 2020): momentum encoder + queue of negatives. Stable longer-batch training.
• **BYOL** (Grill+ 2020): no explicit negatives; predictor + EMA target. Simpler.
• **DINO** (Caron+ 2021): self-distillation + ViT. Emergent attention maps.
• **MAE** (He+ 2021): masked autoencoder; reconstruct masked image patches. Discriminative + generative.
• **CLIP** (Radford+ 2021): image-text contrastive; one of the most important modern models. Image encoder + text encoder; positive pairs from paired (image, caption) data; negatives from other captions. Drives modern multimodal (DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, GPT-4V, LLaVA, etc.).
• **SigLIP** (Zhai+ 2023): sigmoid loss vs softmax; better scaling.

**Why contrastive works**:
1. Self-supervised: no labels needed.
2. Scalable: billions of unlabeled images/texts.
3. Strong representations: linear classifier on frozen features matches supervised.
4. Foundation of multimodal: CLIP embeddings power retrieval + generation.
5. Information-theoretic: maximizes MI between inputs + their representations.

**Connection to other paradigms**:
- Predictive: predict masked or future tokens (BERT, GPT).
- Generative: VAE, diffusion.
- Contrastive: InfoNCE-family.
- Hybrid: increasing common (e.g., MAE + contrastive).

Information-theoretic understanding (InfoNCE = MI bound) drove SSL/contrastive maturation 2018-2023.

question.question: Derive cross-entropy loss for logistic regression
question.goal: Show that minimizing CE on binary outputs equals maximum likelihood for logistic regression.

steps.prompt: Likelihood of single observation P(y | x, θ) for binary y + logistic σ(θ^T x)?
steps.reveal: p = σ(θ^T x). P(y | x, θ) = p^y × (1-p)^(1-y). Bernoulli.
-ℓ = -y log p - (1-y) log(1-p) = binary cross-entropy. **This is the binary CE loss**.

Multi-class: CE = -∑_k y_k log p_k where p = softmax(θ^T x). Direct generalization. Combined with linear-in-θ scores + softmax → optimization-friendly via convex (logistic) or non-convex (neural) optimization. Universal in modern classification.

question.question: Drag the slider to estimate the typical temperature τ used in InfoNCE for SimCLR/CLIP-style contrastive learning.
question.explanation: InfoNCE temperature τ: typically 0.05-0.2 (often 0.07-0.1 for SimCLR + CLIP). Lower τ: sharper softmax over similarities; concentrates loss on hardest negatives. Higher τ: smoother; less discriminative gradient. Hyperparameter tuned empirically. CLIP uses learnable τ (logit scale); ~0.07 at end of training.

question.question: Classify each ML technique by its primary information-theoretic concept.

items.label: PPO with KL constraint to old policy

question.explanation:
Information-theoretic concepts unify ML methods:
• **Cross-entropy / MLE**: standard supervised classification + regression (Gaussian-assumed); REINFORCE policy gradient (log-likelihood × advantage). Optimization-friendly + theoretically optimal under iid sampling.
• **KL / ELBO / variational**: VAEs (ELBO maximization), diffusion models (likelihood-weighted MSE), variational inference, PPO (KL constraint to previous policy, prevents policy collapse).
• **Mutual information / InfoNCE**: SimCLR + MoCo + BYOL (self-supervised contrastive), CLIP + SigLIP + LiT (multimodal contrastive). Maximize MI between augmented views or paired modalities.

All three are facets of the same underlying information-theoretic framework. Modern ML training is multi-component + uses combinations: e.g., RLHF uses cross-entropy (reward model) + KL (constrain policy) + MI (reward model contrastive variants).

question.question: Why has CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining) been so influential since 2021?
options: CLIP demonstrated: (1) contrastive learning on noisy web-scale image-text pairs (400M pairs) creates powerful joint embeddings; (2) zero-shot classification without fine-tuning matches supervised; (3) image + text representations align in shared embedding space; (4) underpins downstream multimodal models — DALL-E 2 + Stable Diffusion + GPT-4V + LLaVA use CLIP encoders or descendants. Showed scale + contrastive learning + open web data produces broadly-useful representations. Influenced LiT, SigLIP, X-CLIP, EVA-CLIP, MetaCLIP successors.
question.explanation:
**CLIP (Radford+ 2021) impact**:

*Technical contributions*:
1. **Contrastive objective**: image encoder + text encoder; positive pairs from (image, caption) in dataset; negatives from other captions in batch. InfoNCE loss.
2. **Web-scale data**: 400M image-text pairs scraped from internet (largely noisy + uncurated).
3. **Modular**: image encoder (ResNet or ViT) + text encoder (transformer); decoupled training.
4. **Zero-shot classification**: 'a photo of [class]' text embeddings → match against image embeddings → classify. No fine-tuning needed.
5. **Linear probe**: frozen features + linear classifier matches supervised on many benchmarks.

*Why so influential*:

(a) **Multimodal embedding space**: aligns image + text in shared latent space. Used by:
- **DALL-E 2** (Ramesh+ 2022): text encoder → CLIP latents → diffusion prior → image decoder.
- **Stable Diffusion** (Rombach+ 2022): text-conditioned diffusion with CLIP encoder.
- **GPT-4V**: vision component uses CLIP-style encoder.
- **LLaVA**: open-source multimodal LLM with CLIP visual encoder.
- **Flamingo** (DeepMind 2022): CLIP-like vision adapter for LLMs.

(b) **Open-world / open-vocabulary**:
- Detection (OWL-ViT, GroundingDINO): CLIP for vocabulary-free object detection.
- Segmentation (LSeg, OpenSeg): CLIP for semantic segmentation.
- Retrieval (image search, video QA): cross-modal retrieval at scale.

(c) **Demonstrating scaling**: showed scaling laws apply to multimodal (more data + compute → better embeddings). Influenced ViT-22B, follow-ups.

(d) **Open ecosystem**:
- Original OpenAI release + many open-source replications (OpenCLIP, MetaCLIP).
- Easy to use embeddings → countless downstream applications.

*Improved variants since 2021*:
- **LiT** (Zhai+ 2022): freeze image encoder, train text on top. Better efficiency.
- **EVA-CLIP** (Sun+ 2023): better data + curriculum; SOTA on benchmarks.
- **SigLIP** (Zhai+ 2023): replace softmax CE with sigmoid; faster + better scaling.
- **X-CLIP** + others: video + audio extensions.
- **MetaCLIP** (Xu+ 2023): improved data curation.
- **DFN-CLIP, DataComp**: data-focused improvements.
- **NVIDIA Sana, OpenAI Sora** etc.: use CLIP-style encoders.

*Lessons*:
1. **Scale + contrastive + web data** produces robust representations.
2. **Multimodal alignment** unlocks generative + retrieval applications.
3. **Open-source releases** enable rapid follow-up research.
4. **Foundation models**: representation learned once + reused across tasks.

CLIP is one of the most influential papers of the 2020-2025 era; foundation of modern multimodal AI.

slides.workedSolution: CLIP (2021): contrastive learning of 400M (image, caption) web pairs creates joint image-text embedding space. Demonstrated: (1) web-scale + contrastive → robust representations; (2) zero-shot classification; (3) shared multimodal latent space. Foundation for DALL-E 2, Stable Diffusion, GPT-4V, LLaVA, Flamingo. Open-world detection (OWL-ViT, GroundingDINO) + segmentation + retrieval. Variants: LiT, EVA-CLIP, SigLIP, MetaCLIP. Influence: scaling laws + multimodal alignment + open-source ecosystem. Foundation model of modern multimodal AI.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why information theory provides a unifying lens for modern ML — from supervised classification to self-supervised representation learning to generative modeling.
question.rubric: Mentions: information theory is the common language of: (1) supervised classification (cross-entropy = KL minimization = MLE); (2) regression (Gaussian assumption → MSE = MLE); (3) variational inference (ELBO maximization = KL minimization vs posterior); (4) generative modeling (likelihood for autoregressive; ELBO for VAE; score-matching for diffusion approximating log p); (5) self-supervised learning (InfoNCE = MI lower bound between views); (6) RL (policy entropy as exploration regularizer; KL constraints in PPO/TRPO); (7) model selection (Akaike, BIC related to entropy); (8) compression-prediction equivalence (Shannon source-coding theorem). Practical impact: cross-entropy loss is universal classification objective; KL constraints stabilize RL; InfoNCE drives modern self-supervised learning; ELBO is foundational for generative models. Information theory provides theoretical guarantees + algorithmic recipes + connection to data + cognitive science (sparse coding, Bayesian brain). Concludes: not a specialized topic; the foundational mathematical theory underlying modern AI.
